dedupe_keys.name: bradford royal infirmary effect of a hospital command centre on emergency department flow and data quality 2018 to 2021

description: This case study evaluates what a hospital command centre, a central room that monitors patient flow and capacity in real time, did to emergency department flow and data quality at Bradford Royal Infirmary in England. The authors, researchers at the Bradford Institute for Health Research, Bradford Teaching Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust, the University of Bradford, the University of Leeds and the University of York, analysed all accident and emergency visits from 1 January 2018 to 31 August 2021 with interrupted time series segmented regression and process mining, and published the work in an open-access journal article. Coverage is one hospital. The article is free to read under a Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial licence; patient records are not public. Caveats: the period overlaps the COVID-19 pandemic, and several interventions were rolled out in sequence. Time from arrival to clinician assessment improved slightly after each stage (by 0.9 to 9.7 minutes), but time from treatment to the end of consultation rose by 11.5 to 53.4 minutes, and data quality results were mixed. Simulation uses: evidence on control room interventions for emergency department flow models and hospital digital twins. Related records: the Newcastle multi-agency incident digital twin (case_study-newcastle-multi-agency-incident-digital-twin) is another operational control room case.
